headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: RisingWave can feed Superset via APIs, but both profiles show no direct shared workspace or sensitive-data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no documented shared communication channel to Superset beyond ordinary APIs, and Superset exposes only its own API surface. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evident by default; the main plausible bridge would be manual copy/paste or an external integration not shown here, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RisingWave-generated text into Superset prompts or dashboards, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, untrusted content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy for any text moved between systems.
Render upstream content as plain text, not executable markup.
Add a provenance label to imported content.
Disable any ad hoc shared folder between the two.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes touched, and RisingWave has no network egress while Superset has allowlisted egress only. Without a shared workspace or known secrets/PII, leakage is not a default-path concern; the remaining risk is limited to operator-created data sharing or future integrations.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a shared workspace containing secrets or PII, leakage risk increases.
IF Superset is configured to query or export data from RisingWave datasets, those contents may flow outward.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid placing secrets in shared input directories.
Review Superset egress allowlist before enabling connectors.
Limit imported datasets to non-sensitive samples.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class tagging and export controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RisingWave is documented as non-runnable here and has no write surfaces listed, while Superset exposes only a Superset API. There is no evidence of overlapping unrestricted filesystem, git, or database writes, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts become possible.
IF a shared database or git repository is introduced, concurrent writes may collide.
mitigations: Keep write access scoped to separate resources.
Do not share a mutable git checkout.
Use per-agent service accounts.
Schedule writes sequentially if a shared target is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can consume API-driven inputs, so RisingWave outputs could become Superset inputs if an operator wires them together. Because no verification workflow is documented, B may treat A's generated data as authoritative by default in an integration, creating a realistic cascading-error path even though the pair is otherwise docs-only.
conditions: IF RisingWave output is imported into Superset without validation, downstream charts or actions may reflect upstream errors.
IF Superset dashboards are used operationally, incorrect upstream data can propagate to decisions.
mitigations: Add a validation step before import.
Mark upstream fields as untrusted.
Require human review for first-run dashboards.
Compare imported aggregates against a known baseline.
requires-engineering: implement schema and freshness checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles show open-source docs-only evidence with no sensitive data classes touched. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, there is no specific pairwise compliance breach to score here.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
IF one agent is configured with a stricter retention policy than the other, mismatch risk may emerge.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Check residency and retention settings.
Avoid regulated data until controls are reviewed.
Keep audit logs for any shared pipeline.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
